First, recall that:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}f(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}({s}^{2}+6) \\ {lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{s}{s-10} \\ {lim}_{s\to 0}{e}^{5s}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}({s}^{2}+6) & ={0}^{2}+6=6\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{s}{s-10} & =\frac{0}{0-10}=0\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}{e}^{5s} & ={e}^{5(0)}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 0}f(s)=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(s)‖$ as $s$ approaches $0$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}‖f(s)‖ & =‖{lim}_{s\to 0}f(s)‖ \\  & =‖[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{37}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the limit ${lim}_{t\to 3}[f(t)\cdot g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2)\,j+t\,k \\ g(t) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2)\,i+\frac{t-{t}^{2}}{1-t}\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}f(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\sqrt{t})\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}t)\,k \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2)\,j+3\,k \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,i+0\,j+3\,k \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,i+3\,k \\ {lim}_{t\to 3}g(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}\frac{t-{t}^{2}}{1-t})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}2)\,k \\  & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}\frac{t(1-t)}{1-t})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}2)\,k \\  & =({lim}_{t\to 3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-2))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 3}t)\,j+({lim}_{t\to 3}2)\,k \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2)\,i+3\,j+2\,k \\  & =0\,i+3\,j+2\,k \\  & =3\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 3}f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to 3}g(t) \\  & =(\sqrt{3}\,i+3\,k)\cdot (3\,j+2\,k) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot 0+0\cdot 3+3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+2g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ \frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{t} \\ \frac{{t}^{2}+4}{t-2}\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t-2 \\ \frac{4t-1}{{t}^{2}-1} \\ {4}^{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of $f(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}2{e}^{t} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{t} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{{t}^{2}+4}{t-2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{0} \\ 0 \\ \frac{{0}^{2}+4}{0-2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The limit of a second component here was found using L'Hopital's Rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{t} & ={lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{′}}{{t}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡0}{1} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limit of $g(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}(2t-2) \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{4t-1}{{t}^{2}-1} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}{4}^{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2(0)-2 \\ \frac{4(0)-1}{{0}^{2}-1} \\ {4}^{0}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+2g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)+2{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, recall that:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}f(s) & =⟨{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡{s}^{2}}{s-1},\,{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{6s-\operatorname{sin}⁡(s-1)}{3s-2},\,{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{{s}^{3}+4s-2}{{s}^{2}+s-1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- The first component can be found using L'Hopital's Rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡{s}^{2}}{s-1} & ={lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡s}{s-1} \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{(2\operatorname{ln}⁡s)^{′}}{(s-1)^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{(\frac{2}{s})}{1} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{6s-\operatorname{sin}⁡(s-1)}{3s-2} & =\frac{6(1)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(1-1)}{3(1)-2} \\  & =\frac{6-0}{1} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{{s}^{3}+4s-2}{{s}^{2}+s-1} & =\frac{(1)^{3}+4(1)-2}{(1)^{2}+(1)-1} \\  & =\frac{3}{1} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)=⟨2,\,6,\,3⟩.$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(s)‖$ as $s$ approaches $1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}‖f(s)‖ & =‖{lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)‖ \\  & =‖⟨2,\,6,\,3⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+36+9} \\  & =\sqrt{49} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)-2g(t)]$ given that
$f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨1+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{t}^{2}-1,\,\frac{4+t}{2-{t}^{2}}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{2},\,\sqrt{t}+\sqrt{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\,(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}\,({t}^{2}-1),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{4+t}{2-{t}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨1+\operatorname{sin}⁡0,{0}^{2}-1,\frac{4+0}{2-{0}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{1}{2},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}\,(\sqrt{t}+\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\frac{1}{2},\sqrt{0}+\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\frac{1}{2},\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)-2g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)-{lim}_{t\to 0}2g(t) \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)-2{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩-2⟨1,\frac{1}{2},\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩-⟨2,1,2\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨1-2,-1-1,2-2\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-2,2-2\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
